acceptance: No published doc, CLI output or Explorer string claims TPC compliance, certification or official status for a BenchBox run
The derived-results disclaimer appears with TPC results in docs, CLI reports and Explorer charts
Power@Size and Throughput@Size keep their names
context: Core repo delivered in merged PR #3435: TPC-H 'certification report' is now a validation report, TPC-DS compliance report a validation checklist report, 'Official TPC-DS Metrics' headings 'derived metrics'; CLI run-mode prompt, --official help, banners and scale-factor errors no longer say TPC-compliant; a 'Derived from <benchmark>... does not comply with the Specification ... must not be compared with official results' disclaimer is on reports (text/HTML/CSV), the audit trail, `benchbox metrics qphh` and the official-mode banner; docs reworded. Kept: Power@Size/Throughput@Size names, routed/official/unofficial result-class vocabulary, publish/submit refusal text; legacy names ValidationLevel.CERTIFICATION/CertificationChecker/certification_status remain with reworded messages. STILL OPEN in other repos: Explorer/site text (TrustBadge.tsx wording, Explorer chart disclaimer) and blog draft 18 (benchbox-site). Item stays open for those.
description: BenchBox text claims more than an unaudited run supports. The TPC Fair Use Quick Reference (v1.0.0, 2019) requires derived results to be labelled "Derived from <benchmark>", carry a disclaimer that they "do not comply with the <benchmark> Specification", and never be compared with official results. Remove: "certification-ready" (docs/guides/tpc/tpc-h-official-guide.md ~12, ~643; tpc-ds-official-guide.md ~12, ~850); the "TPC-H BENCHMARK CERTIFICATION REPORT ... ready for certification submission" output (benchbox/core/tpch/reporting.py ~121-195); "TPC-compliant" and "is compliant" in the run-mode prompt (benchbox/cli/benchmarks.py ~855-901) and banners (run.py ~549-558, ~1117-1137); "Official TPC-H/DS Metrics" headings (docs/benchmarks/tpc-h.md ~112, tpc-ds.md ~333); "Running TPC-H compliant benchmarks"; and similar in docs/contributing-results.md, publish.py, submit.py, blog draft 18. Keep "official" only for the TPC's own spec, tools, website and audited results. Owner decision 2026-10-08: keep the Power@Size and Throughput@Size names, with the derived-results disclaimer. Add the disclaimer wherever results and charts are shown (docs, CLI reports, Explorer).
